maya: Heads-up — while running the kernel-selection benchmark with the episodic burst generator I keep seeing a 99.9th tail that only appears when bursts are spaced irregularly. Need a quick sync on how we should validate this and avoid chasing flaky noise.
ben: Can you paste the generator config and the exact run command?
maya: Sure — minimal config below. This is using `burst_mode: episodic` with Pareto interarrival for the long tail. Ran on top-of-tree runtime with kernel auto-select enabled.
```
# synthetic generator config
mode: episodic
seed: 1623
burst_profile:
  episodes_per_minute: 2
  burst_size_mean: 40
  burst_size_sigma: 10
  within_burst_qps: 600
interarrival: pareto
pareto_shape: 1.8
kv_warmup: 0.6
batching:
  max_batch_ms: 8
  target_tokens_per_batch: 128
```
maya: Command was `./harness replay --config episodic.yml --targets=10 --duration=20m --save=run-1863`

hugo: Quick thought — Pareto with shape <2 gives a heavy tail for gaps; that could create long cold starts for KV if gaps exceed the TTL. Are you seeing cold-KV misses correlated with tail latencies?
sasha: @maya can you share the perf profile slice for a high-tail request (cpu + kernel selection logs)? Even a short snippet helps.
maya: Pasted the hot path excerpt — kernel choose selects int8 kernel, then falls back to fp16 for one microbatch due to kernel memory mismatch, then reselects int8 for the rest. That's the weird flip.
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] choose_kernel(model=v1, seq=128) -> kernel=int8_optimized
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] kv_cache: found prefix, hit_rate=0.72
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] execute: alloc failed on int8_optimized microbatch 2 -> fallback fp16
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] reselect kernel=int8_optimized after reclaim
[2026-03-17T14:02:13Z] latent_tail_ms = 472
```
ben: That fallback/reselect loop would explain spikes — memory fragmentation across episodic bursts maybe. If the episodic generator produces tightly-packed bursts then large idle gaps, allocator heuristics might fragment.
qa-lead: Also ensure the replay harness uses the same warmup sequence as the real traffic. Our apples-to-apples rule: 1) identical prefix distribution, 2) identical KV hit/miss pattern by replaying exact trace or seeded generator, 3) same batching bucket parameters.
hugo: Propose two validation steps: A) deterministic replay of real traces (from prod sampling) to ensure baseline parity, B) synthetic episodic stress with controlled interarrival distributions (expo, poisson, pareto, lognormal) to exercise tails and allocator behavior.
sasha: For allocator repros I'd add an experiment toggling kv_warmup levels and GC thresholds to see sensitivity. Keep other knobs fixed.
maya: Agreed. I'm worried our current generator conflates burst shape and total QPS. Need a way to sculpt long-tail latency while keeping mean QPS constant. Any ideas?
ben: We use a two-stage controller in our other harnesses: base-rate controller maintains mean QPS, burst-injector overlays episodic bursts sampled from a shaped distribution. That keeps total tokens consistent.

maya: Can you sketch parameters?
ben: Example pattern: base_qps=100, overlay episodes with amplitude A chosen so that integrated extra load per minute = target. Episodes follow Weibull for within-burst spacing and Pareto for inter-episode gap to get fat gap tails.

ben: Here's a sample generator invocation we should try: `./synth --base-qps 120 --episodes 3/m --episode-qps 700 --episode-duration 6s --interepisode=p:1.9 --seed 42`

perf-bot: [automated] note: previous run (seed=42) produces 99.9th latency 480ms; baseline deterministic replay 99.9th 210ms.

maya: Good to know. I'll run the overlay model with a few seeds and collect kernel-selection traces and allocator stats.

sasha: When comparing runs, use token-normalized metrics: per-token p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and also report kernel-change counts (how many reselects per 10k requests). That will surface flapping kernels.
hugo: And log KV cache TTL and miss counters per-request. If episodic gaps exceed TTL, you'll see KV miss spikes aligning with tails.

maya: One more tricky bit — batching heuristics. In burst mode we often hit max_batch_ms, which increases microbatching and potentially triggers the fallback due to transient memory pressure. We should test both conservative and aggressive batching configs.

ben: Right — plan experiments matrix: interarrival distribution x kv_warmup x batching_max_ms (4 values) x seed (3 seeds). Keep run length >15m to get stable tails.

qa-lead: Please tag runs with metadata: release-hash, kernel-build, node-image, allocator-version. We'll need that to triage non-deterministic flips.

maya: I'll kick off the matrix tonight. If anyone has a short checklist for extracting the kernel reselect trace and a small extraction script, please drop it here. Trying to keep the first run quick. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sasha: Use this one-liner to extract reselects from the runtime log: `grep -E \"reselect kernel|alloc failed\" runtime.log | awk '{print $1 " " $5 " " $7}' > reselects.csv`

hugo: Also capture a per-node allocator fragmentation snapshot after each episode: `./allocator snapshot --out frag-$(runid).json`

maya: Thanks — will post results and a short summary. If we see consistent kernel flaps tied to batching_max_ms, we should consider a quick mitigation: pin kernel selection when microbatch count > 1 for a short grace window to avoid flip-flopping during bursts.

ben: Good mitigation idea. Could also add a small backoff before reselecting to drain transient pressure.

maya: OK launching. Will report back with p99/p99.9 trends + kernel-change rates and KV miss alignment. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
